title: platform-standup-2026-03-28
content:
Platform Engineering — Standup notes (2026-03-28)
Owners: Maya Chen (notes), Alejandro Ruiz (routing), Priya Nair (auth/quotas), Samir Patel (control plane)
Attendees: Maya, Alejandro, Priya, Samir, Hannah, Shaun (SRE)

TL;DR:
- Canary rollout for new routing policy in us-west-2 started yesterday; initial metrics look OK but saw spike in 429s for a small subset of customers. Investigating.
- Quota enforcement bug (double-counting reserved capacity on Dedicated nodes) root cause identified; hotfix PR queued.
- Control plane autoscaler: improving backoff logic to avoid thrash during noisy neighbor events; simulation results positive.
- Auth: migrating token introspection cache TTL from 30s->60s to reduce load; monitoring for auth drift.

Last week / Yesterday
- Routing: Alejandro finished core of model-variant routing update (PR #288). Integration tests passed in CI, started canary at 10% traffic to canary pool in us-west-2 yesterday afternoon.
  - Observed 95th p50/p95 latency within expected range for canary pool.
  - Noticed a ~3% increase in 429 rate for legacy clients (older client versions still sending endpoint X). Likely mismatch in header parsing logic in fallback path.
  - Action: Alejandro to roll a targeted patch to fallback path and re-run canary. (Blocked briefly by test harness flake)
- Quotas/Auth: Priya found quota accounting edge-case where reserved capacity decrement runs twice during eviction path on Dedicated nodes — this led to transient over-promising of tokens for a few customers.
  - Root cause: race between eviction handler and reservation cleanup job.
  - Hotfix PR created targeting the reservation cleanup ordering. PR links in artifacts.
- Control plane: Samir ran load test with new autoscaler backoff configuration. Under synthetic noisy-neighbor traffic, we saw >40% reduction in scale-up oscillations. Still tuning thresholds for 99th percentile CPU bursts.
- Observability: Hannah added per-route token-level metrics to the console dashboard for canary customers; useful for quick triage.

Today / This week
- Routing (Alejandro): finish patch for header parsing fallback; re-run canary at 20% if patch looks good. Timeline: EOD 2026-03-29 to deploy patch to canary.
- Quotas (Priya): merge hotfix and schedule emergency deploy to Dedicated staging cluster. Putting on-call SRE (Shaun) in loop for rollback plan.
- Control plane (Samir): tune autoscaler hold-time and retry logic; run 6-hour soak in staging. Aim to promote to canary next week.
- Auth (Priya/Hannah): monitor token TTL change after deploy; look for any SSO/provider errors. If see drift >0.5% of auth failures, revert TTL change.
- Observability/Playbooks (Maya): update playbook for quota overcommit incident with steps and quick checks. Draft ready, need review.

Blockers / Risks
- 429 spike for legacy clients could be more widespread if fallback patch doesn't fully address header parsing mismatch. Risk: customer-facing errors. Priority: high.
- Quota hotfix needs thorough e2e testing; if merged without guardrails might cause other timing-sensitive paths to regress. Mitigation: deploy with feature flag and ramp.
- Autoscaler tuning still has unknowns under multi-tenant burst patterns; range of parameter values appears narrow — risk of oscillation if mis-tuned.

Action items / Owners
- Alejandro: finish fallback header parsing patch, add regression test for legacy client header shape, re-run canary. (Due: 2026-03-29)
- Priya: finalize reserve cleanup hotfix PR, schedule Dedicated staging deploy, coordinate with SRE for deploy window and rollback plan. (Due: 2026-03-29)
- Samir: finalize autoscaler hold-time tuning and start 6-hour soak in staging; produce soak report. (Due: 2026-03-31)
- Hannah: add alert for token-level 429 spikes scoped to canary customers; verify dashboard panels include new metrics. (Due: 2026-03-30)
- Maya: publish quota incident playbook draft to Confluence and ping CS/Support for runbook review. (Due: 2026-03-30)

Open questions / Notes to follow up
- Should we add a compatibility header-check layer in the routing gateway to normalize legacy clients? Pros: centralizes fix. Cons: adds extra hop/latency. Tentative: prototype and measure. (Alejandro)
- Quota accounting: consider switching reservation cleanup to a transactional queue to avoid races. More invasive — add to backlog for Q2 work. (Priya/Samir)
- Autoscaler: explore predictive smoothing based on workload series (simple AR(1) vs moving-average). If promising, prototyping in April. (Samir/Applied-ML)

Incidents / Customer Impact
- Small cohort of Dedicated customers experienced transient quota miscount -> brief over-allocation followed by forced throttling. No data loss. CS notified; customer-facing notes drafted by Support. Root cause identified and hotfix in PR.

Meeting notes / decisions
- Decision: proceed with targeted fallback patch first rather than a large compatibility layer. Faster remediation and lower risk.
- Decision: deploy quota hotfix to Dedicated staging behind feature flag; monitor for 2 hours before promoting to production.

Files / refs mentioned
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/288
- JIRA: PLAT-412 (routing header fallback), PLAT-421 (quota double-counting)
- Confluence: Quota Design and incident playbook (link above)

Misc quick notes / scratchpad
- Reminder: internal demo of new per-token billing dashboard next Wed 2026-04-01; need sample dataset from billing team. (Maya)
- Spike: look into adding per-customer fallback weight control in routing policy UI — low priority. (Product request from CS)

Next standup: 2026-03-29 09:30 PT

Maya Chen
Platform Engineering
